title: Buying a Gaming Laptop Before GTA 6 Comes to PC? Here's How I'd Choose
summary: GTA 6 isn't confirmed for PC yet, but if you're buying a gaming laptop now, here's why VRAM and GPU tier matter most, plus the models I'd shortlist.
body_markdown:
Rockstar's GTA VI launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026. A PC version hasn't been announced. On October 13, 2026, GamesBeat reported a PC release planned for the first quarter of 2027, citing four anonymous sources, and Rockstar hasn't commented publicly. So if you're buying a gaming laptop now with GTA VI in mind, you're really buying for unknown requirements.


That shapes how I'd pick. Since nobody knows the specs, I'd buy for headroom where it's hardest to add later: the GPU tier and its video memory. A laptop's GPU can't be upgraded, so it's the one decision you live with.


## Why VRAM matters more in a laptop


Laptop GPU names don't mean the same thing as desktop ones. According to the spec tables on these listings, the RTX 5060 and RTX 5070 laptop GPUs here have 8GB of VRAM, the RTX 5070 Ti laptop GPU has 12GB, and the RTX 5080 laptop GPU has 16GB. For big open-world games, 8GB is where texture settings start to get uncomfortable. That's why I'd treat the RTX 5070 Ti laptop as the sweet spot if your budget allows it.


Power limits matter too. Two laptops with the same GPU can perform differently depending on how much power and cooling the maker gives it. Reviews that test the specific model are worth reading before buying.

## My picks


**Best balance:** the[MSI Vector 16 HX AI](https://www.newegg.com/p/2WC-000C-0JJ10?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) pairs an RTX 5070 Ti laptop GPU with a Core Ultra 7 255HX and two Thunderbolt 5 ports. The 512GB SSD is small for modern games, so I'd plan on adding storage.


**Best big screen:** the[Acer Predator Helios Neo 18 AI](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16834360388?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) gives you the same GPU tier on an 18-inch 2560x1600 240Hz panel with a Core Ultra 9 275HX. It's a desk machine more than a backpack one, but that screen is a treat for open-world games.


**Most memory out of the box:** the[GIGABYTE Gaming A16 PRO](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIB32ZKST4596?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) comes with 32GB and a 1TB SSD alongside its RTX 5070 Ti and a 2560x1600 165Hz display.


**Midrange:** the[Acer Nitro V 16S AI](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16834360451?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) uses an RTX 5070 laptop GPU with 8GB and DDR5-6400. Its spec table lists both memory slots as filled with 32GB as the maximum, so it's worth knowing that before you buy.


## Budget picks


If the budget is firm, RTX 5060 laptops are the entry point. The[Acer Nitro V16](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16834360411?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) stands out because it ships with 32GB of RAM, which is more than most laptops in this tier. The[ASUS TUF Gaming 16 with a Ryzen 7 260](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16834236758?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) lists a single 16GB stick with one slot open, so adding a second stick is an easy upgrade. The[MSI Cyborg A15](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16834156974?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) is a 15.6-inch 144Hz option with a 1TB SSD.


I'd go in with realistic expectations here. An 8GB laptop GPU will likely need lower texture settings in the next wave of big games, and that's fine as long as you know it going in.


## If money isn't the issue


The[MSI Raider 18](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIA24GKJX2068?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gaming-laptop-before-gta-6-pc-buying-guide) is the most powerful option on this list, with an RTX 5080 laptop GPU and 16GB of VRAM, a Ryzen 9 9955HX3D, 32GB of DDR5 with two slots open, a 2TB Gen5 SSD and an 18-inch 3840x2400 Mini LED panel. It's heavy and expensive, but it's the one I'd expect to age most gracefully.


## What I'd check in reviews before buying


Spec tables don't tell the whole story with laptops, so I look for a few things in reviews of the exact model. **GPU power limit:** makers set different maximum power for the same GPU, and a higher limit usually means more performance if the cooling keeps up. **Display switching:** a MUX switch or NVIDIA Advanced Optimus lets the GPU drive the screen directly, which can help frame rates. **Fan noise under load:** some laptops are much louder than others at full tilt.


I'd also look at practical details. The MSI Vector 16 HX AI uses a 330W charger according to its listing, and the GIGABYTE Gaming A16 PRO a 240W one, which tells you these are plug-in machines for gaming. Battery life while gaming will be short on any of them. Storage expansion is worth checking too, since a second M.2 slot makes it easy to add space for big games without replacing the original drive.


Finally, think about where you'll play. An 18-inch laptop like the Helios Neo 18 AI or Raider 18 is great on a desk and a chore in a backpack. A 16-inch model is the more flexible size for most people.


## Final verdict


If GTA VI on PC is the main reason you're shopping, there's no rush, since nothing is confirmed. If you need a laptop now anyway, prioritize the GPU tier and VRAM, then plan to add RAM or storage later where the laptop allows it. The RTX 5070 Ti laptops hit the best balance for me.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is GTA 6 coming to PC?** Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version. GamesBeat reported on October 13, 2026 that a PC release is planned for the first quarter of 2027, citing anonymous sources.


**How much VRAM should a gaming laptop have for future games?** I'd aim for at least 12GB if you want to run high texture settings in large open-world games for the next few years. The RTX 5070 Ti laptop GPU has 12GB.


**Is an RTX 5060 laptop good enough for new games?** It can run new games well at 1080p, but its 8GB of VRAM means you may need to lower texture quality in the most demanding titles.


**Can I upgrade a gaming laptop's GPU later?** No. Laptop GPUs are soldered to the motherboard, which is why choosing the right GPU tier up front matters most.


**Can I add more RAM to these laptops?** Some, yes. Check the listing's spec table for open memory slots. Some models ship with all slots filled or with soldered memory.
